analysis: What changed versus the 6:00 AM brief: the mixed premarket tape resolved into a split open — Dow -0.6% while S&P +0.2% and Nasdaq +0.6% — rather than the uniformly soft S&P read in IBD's later premarket update. Oil also flipped: the premarket rebound to ~$97.50 faded to ~$96.15 at the open, removing one headwind. Shopify narrowed its drop from ~16% premarket to ~10% in morning action, the clearest early sign that selling pressure is easing off the lows, while Apple and Palantir held their ~4% and 6%+ declines. Megacaps mostly firmed in early trading (Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet up; Tesla slightly down), which is why the Nasdaq could rise despite Apple's Dow drag. Signal vs noise: AMD after the bell, the 10:00 a.m. ET JOLTS/factory-orders data, and the USAC call at 11:00 a.m. ET are today's real catalysts; midterm odds are positioning chatter until results land overnight. The sell-the-beat pattern remains the dominant theme, but the chip bounce and Shopify's partial recovery argue against reading the open as a broad risk-off session.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Split open on Election Day (IBD live coverage, just after the open): Dow -0.6%, S&P 500 +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.6%; SPY +0.2%, QQQ +0.6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket split carried into the open — blue-chip drag from Apple, tech stabilization from chips, no broad risk-on or risk-off read yet.

headlines.headline: Apple sold off on its margin guide: down ~4% at the open, set to open at its lowest since Sept. 10, despite fiscal Q4 EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 expected and sales $114.5B vs $113.4B expected; December-quarter gross margin guided to 45-46% vs 47.9% in September, with rising memory costs cited (IBD/Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat sold on guidance again — memory-cost pressure into the holiday quarter is the price driver, not the September beat.

headlines.headline: Chips bounced at the open: Nvidia up nearly 3% premarket, on pace to snap a four-day losing streak; Sandisk jumped nearly 7% and Monolithic Power over 5% among Nasdaq-100 leaders just after the open (IBD). AMD, up ~3-4% premarket, reports after the close (EPS $1.95 on $13.1B expected).
headlines.why_it_matters: The most beaten-down group is leading the early tape — AMD's print after the bell decides whether this is a bounce or a reversal.

headlines.headline: Palantir tumbled 6%+ at the open after beating Q3 earnings and revenue targets, as new contract growth slowed; on pace for a sixth straight losing session after breaking its 50-day line Monday (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Another beat sold on a deceleration metric — valuation names are being charged for any slowing growth signal.

headlines.headline: Shopify plunged nearly 10% in morning action (IBD), narrowing from its ~16% premarket drop after Q3 revenue of $3.74B matched consensus; Thomson Reuters fell almost 12% and Dynatrace nearly 14%, while Ferrari rose 2%+ and Yum Brands jumped close to 4%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The sell-the-beat pattern is broad but easing off premarket lows — early-session recovery in Shopify is a sentiment tell for the rest of the morning.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split in early trading (Finnhub/MarketBeat live quotes): Meta +1.07%, Microsoft +0.82%, Amazon +0.41%, Alphabet +0.6%, Tesla -0.42% versus Monday's close.
headlines.why_it_matters: No single megacap direction — most names firming offsets Tesla softness, consistent with the split index tape.

headlines.headline: Archer-Daniels-Midland beat Q3 estimates and raised its full-year guide: adjusted EPS $1.77 vs $1.60 expected (LSEG), FY 2026 adjusted EPS forecast raised to $5.50-$5.80 from $5.15-$5.60, on stronger oilseed processing margins; ag services and oilseeds operating profit more than doubled to $778M (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: Raised guidance — a counterweight to the sell-the-beat tape, showing margin stories outside tech are still getting rewarded.

headlines.headline: Midterms today, macro at 10:00 a.m. ET: September JOLTS job openings (7.1M expected vs 7.09M prior) and factory orders (+1.1% expected vs +0.1% prior); polls favor Democrats retaking the House, Polymarket puts Democrats at 78% for the Senate and 95% for the House (IBD). Oil eased to ~$96.15 WTI at the open after the premarket rebound faded.
headlines.why_it_matters: Results emerge overnight, so traders carry election risk with no scheduled announcement to trade against; the 10:00 a.m. ET data is the next scheduled catalyst.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq-100 still in correction: Monday's close was more than 10% below its October 6 record, its third correction of 2026, with the semiconductor benchmark down ~12% in three sessions (carried from the 6:00 AM brief).
headlines.why_it_matters: Correction status frames every tech bounce as guilty-until-proven-innocent — AMD after the bell is the next proof point.

usac.headline: USA Compression Partners reported Q3 2026 results this morning: revenue $357.2M (vs $250.3M a year ago and ~$348.32M consensus), Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, distribution held at $0.525; shares opened at $24.80, flat to Monday's $24.80 close (-2.71% Monday). Conference call at 11:00 a.m. ET today; $0.525 distribution pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26.
usac.why_it_matters: A revenue beat that has not yet moved the quote — the 11:00 a.m. ET call is the next chance for the print to translate into price action.
